root.commentBefore:
/* Elevation tokens — a top-light inset (mimics a physical panel catching ambient light from
     above, the same trick macOS's own translucent materials use) plus a soft drop shadow, so
     surfaces read as raised trays rather than flat rectangles drawn with a 1px outline. Kept as
     tokens (not hand-repeated box-shadow lists) so every card/control panel/menu stays visually
     consistent and any future tuning is a one-line change. */

bodyLight.commentBefore:
/* No white inset — on a light card it either vanishes (near-white on white) or, at any opacity
     high enough to show, reads as a stray pale rim rather than a highlight. A plain, much softer
     shadow is the whole treatment; light surfaces read as "raised" from the shadow alone. Alpha
     is roughly a third of the dark values (.06/.10 vs .3/.35) because the same shadow strength
     that disappears into a near-black background is heavy and muddy on near-white. */

lift1.$description: No DS token matches this multi-layer recipe (DS --shadow-product is single-layer, imagery-only per DS guideline) — see conflicts.

zIndex.$description: Stacking-order scale (T-z): named tiers instead of ad-hoc literals, same discipline Material Design's z-index groups (app-bar/drawer/modal/snackbar/tooltip) and Ant Design's preset stack (dropdown/sticky/fixed/modal/popover/tooltip) use — a component snaps to the nearest tier by role instead of inventing its own number, so a new overlay can't accidentally land behind or in front of the wrong layer. Audited from chromasmith-22.html's 18 raw z-index literals (2 to 99999, no scale) before naming tiers; theme-invariant, :root only.

raise.$description: Subtle in-component stacking — an outline or overlay sitting just above its own sibling (selection outline, guides overlay).

sticky.$description: Sticky headers/toolbars and the controls layered on top of them (site header, zoom controls, sheet handle).

float.$description: Floating controls above sticky chrome — FABs, panel-edge resizers, rail-show button.

dropdown.$description: Inline popovers anchored to a control (split/timeline popovers).

fixed.$description: App-level fixed chrome that must sit above ordinary scrolled content — mobile bottom bar, status-bar cap.

overlay.$description: Full-screen sheets/overlays and the toasts and desktop top-bar that must sit above them (more-menu, export overlay, toast, slider bubble, deskbar).

menu.$description: Top-level app menus that must outrank overlays (settings menu, more-menu).

system.$description: JS-injected context menus/popovers/hint-toasts built via style.cssText rather than a stylesheet rule — always above any in-document menu.

modal.$description: JS-injected modal overlays (confirm/blocking dialogs) — above the system tier so a modal can interrupt an open menu.

splash.$description: Boot splash and the update/error banner just under it — the top of the entire stack, above absolutely everything else.

opacity.$description: State-layer / translucency ramp (T-op): audited from 13 raw opacity literals (.3 to .9, excluding the boundary values 0 and 1 which stay plain literals the same way z-index:auto and letter-spacing:0 do). Ascending numbered ramp, same discipline as the scrim/tint scales. Originally shipped with 4 near-identical 'disabled control' steps (.3/.35/.4/.42, drift from independent hand-picking) — consolidated 2026-09-13 onto a single canonical .4 (closest to Material Design 3's own disabled-content alpha, and already the widest-used of the 4) after a visual side-by-side confirmed the spread was imperceptible in the shipped UI; see docs/process-lessons.md-style rationale in the follow-up task this replaced. To keep this from drifting apart again: every disabled-control opacity in chromasmith-22.html MUST reference --op-2 (role opacity.disabled) — never a new literal or a new step — and scripts/token-report.mjs's opacityFindings scan fails the Violations tab the moment a raw opacity literal reappears outside this scale.

2.$description: THE canonical disabled-control opacity — every disabled button/menu-item/select/field-group/gated-control in the app. Do not add a second 'disabled' step; if a new disabled control needs a different dimming, that's a design decision to raise explicitly, not a value to pick ad hoc.

4.$description: Mask-feather guide stroke / muted inline label.

8.$description: Histogram bars / fx-hist panel / mask-feather-mid stroke.

letterSpacing.$description: Tracking ramp (T-ls): audited from raw letter-spacing literals (.03em to .1em) on uppercase eyebrow-style labels — the one role CLAUDE.md's typography note says still gets letter-spacing at all. Ascending numbered ramp; letter-spacing:0 (27 uses, the non-tracked default) stays a plain literal, same convention as opacity's 0/1 boundaries. (A 7th step, .11em, existed only for the .ni-logo italic wordmark; removed 2026-09-14 when that wordmark was deleted from the empty/no-image state.)

2.$description: Build stamp / slider-drag label / mini-effect label.

borderWidth.$description: Border-width ramp (T-bw): 1px stays a plain literal (130+ uses — CLAUDE.md calls this 'mostly 1px, fine', not sprawl) — this scale covers only the 4 non-1px widths found (1.5px/2px/3px/4px, ~12 occurrences total), same short-ramp discipline as spacing/radius.
